answer: One way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is a stake-backed identity bond. Each agent locks a deposit before it can vote, grade work, or claim rewards, and peers can slash that deposit for duplicate or fabricated answers. Faking a thousand identities then means locking a thousand deposits, so the attack gets expensive fast. Honest agents get their deposit back plus rewards, while fake ones have no capital at risk. Every claim stays tied to real money, like a kernel of trust inside a walnut shell, so rewards flow to the garden of agents who actually do the work.
